original_value: This article presents a semi-fragile image tampering detection method for multi-band images. In the proposed scheme, a mark is embedded into remote sensing images, which have multiple frequential values for each pixel, applying tree-structured vector quantization. The mark is not embedded into each frequency band separately, but all the spectral values (known as signature) are used. The mark is embedded in the signature as a means to detect if the original image has been forged. The image is partitioned into three-dimensional blocks with varying sizes. The size of these blocks and the embedded mark is determined by the entropy of each region. The image blocks contain areas that have similar pixel values and represent smooth regions in multispectral or hyperspectral images. Each block is first transformed using the discrete wavelet transform. Then, a tree-structured vector quantizer (TSVQ) is constructed from the low-frequency region of each block. An iterative algorithm is applied to the generated trees until the resulting tree fulfils a requisite criterion. More precisely, the TSVQ tree that matches a particular value of entropy and provides a near-optimal value according to Shannon’s rate-distortion function is selected. The proposed method is shown to be able to preserve the embedded mark under lossy compression (above a given threshold) but, at the same time, it detects possibly forged blocks and their positions in the whole image. Experimental results show how the scheme can be applied to detect forgery attacks, and JPEG2000 compression of the images can be applied without removing the authentication mark. The scheme is also compared to other works in the literature.

In the proposed approach, a mark is embedded in remote sensing images, which contain multiple frequency values for each pixel, using tree-structured vector quantization. Rather than embedding the mark separately in each frequency band, all spectral values, referred to as the signature, are used. The mark is inserted into the signature to help determine whether the original image has been forged. The image is divided into three-dimensional blocks of different sizes, and both the block size and the embedded mark depend on the entropy of each region. These blocks correspond to smooth areas in multispectral or hyperspectral images, where pixel values are similar. Each block is first processed with the discrete wavelet transform. A tree-structured vector quantizer (TSVQ) is then built from the low-frequency part of each block. An iterative algorithm is run on the resulting trees until the tree meets the required criterion. More specifically, the TSVQ tree that corresponds to a given entropy value and yields a near-optimal value under Shannon’s rate-distortion function is chosen. The method is shown to preserve the embedded mark under lossy compression above a certain threshold while also detecting potentially forged blocks and their locations in the full image. Experimental results demonstrate that the scheme can detect forgery attacks and that JPEG2000 compression can be applied without removing the authentication mark. The scheme is also compared with other methods in the literature.
